gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the scanners in its suggested bundles are rated under different, non-comparable conditions. Creality rates the Otter Lite at 0.05 mm at 100 mm on a 100 mm sphere pair and the Otter at 0.02 mm at 60 mm. 3DMakerpro gives the Moose Lite's 0.05 mm with no test condition. Creality's page gives only 'Accuracy 0.1mm' for the Ferret SE. None of the four publishes a volumetric accuracy, the figure that tells you whether a full-size replacement part will fit. The specs that do compare cleanly are minimum object size (Otter 10 mm cube, Otter Lite 20 mm cube) and 3D resolution (Otter 0.05 mm, Otter Lite 0.1 mm, Moose Lite 0.10 mm, Ferret SE 0.16 mm).
standout_why: Compared against the cited Creality pages (the scanner-combo collection and the K2 Plus combo page), 3dprintmates.com and rottenwifi.com. The Creality pages state no scanner specs at all, and the K2 Plus combo page doesn't even name its scanner. 3dprintmates uses accuracy and precision as interchangeable terms and never mentions volumetric accuracy. RottenWiFi explains single-frame vs volumetric accuracy and resolution vs accuracy, but only in general terms. For the Ferret SE it gives 0.1 mm accuracy and 0.16 mm resolution, and it gives no figures or test conditions for the Otter or Otter Lite. It does not cover the Moose Lite, and it never points out that none of these four publishes a volumetric figure. None of the pages gives minimum scan volumes. RottenWiFi already covers part of this (the concept and the Ferret SE figures), so the table's value is in the product-by-product test conditions and minimum sizes.
decides: ChatGPT's answer suggests 'better scanning quality' rises with price, but the headline accuracy figures can't rank these four. Each was measured at a different distance or on a different object, or the condition isn't given, and none gives volumetric accuracy. The specs that do separate them for copying small replacement parts are minimum scannable size and 3D resolution. The Otter (10 mm cube, 0.05 mm resolution) can handle smaller and finer parts than the Otter Lite in the $1,606 combo ChatGPT showed (20 mm cube, 0.1 mm). The Ferret SE in the budget pairing is coarsest at 0.16 mm. So for small mechanical parts, spend on the Otter rather than the Otter Lite. For figurines and household objects bigger than 20 mm, the Otter Lite or Moose Lite is enough.
